# Blinkql

> Blinkql is an open-source SQL workbench that runs entirely in the browser, for files too big for a spreadsheet and too sensitive to upload: CSV, Parquet and JSON exports of 1–2 million rows, and Excel workbooks. Queries run locally, and files never leave the user's computer. Version 1.0 is out; it was built in the open across eight milestones.

The workbench is at https://blinkql.karthik.nz/app/. Licensed under MIT. Built by Karthik Parameshwara (https://karthik.nz/).

## Docs

How to use the workbench, at https://blinkql.karthik.nz/docs/.

- [Get started](https://blinkql.karthik.nz/docs/get-started/): Open the workbench, load sample data or your own file, and run your first query.
- [Open files](https://blinkql.karthik.nz/docs/open-files/): Open CSV, TSV, Excel, Parquet and JSON files from your computer or a web address, and keep them between visits.
- [Write queries](https://blinkql.karthik.nz/docs/write-queries/): Write SQL with autocomplete, run all or part of a query, cancel it, fix errors and find past queries.
- [Explore results](https://blinkql.karthik.nz/docs/explore-results/): Scroll through results, profile a table's columns and chart what a query returns.
- [Analysis templates](https://blinkql.karthik.nz/docs/templates/): Run ready-made analyses such as OEE and downtime Pareto on sample data or your own files.
- [Share and export](https://blinkql.karthik.nz/docs/share-and-export/): Export results and charts, save an analysis as an HTML report, and share a query as a link.
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://blinkql.karthik.nz/docs/keyboard-shortcuts/): Every keyboard shortcut in the workbench, grouped by where it works.
- [Privacy and storage](https://blinkql.karthik.nz/docs/privacy-and-storage/): What stays on your computer, what the browser keeps between visits, and how to remove it.
- [Browser support and limits](https://blinkql.karthik.nz/docs/browser-support/): Which browsers Blinkql supports, how large a file it handles, and what to do when something doesn't work.
